subject.title: [Bug]: OpenAI-compatible streaming tool calls are dropped when provider omits finish_reason

question: Should OpenClaw treat native OpenAI-compatible `delta.tool_calls` plus a clean raw SSE `[DONE]` terminal as sufficient to execute tools when the provider omits final `finish_reason`?
rationale: This changes a shipped fail-closed tool-execution boundary for custom providers, and automation cannot decide that product/security contract without maintainer intent.

options.title: Accept clean-DONE tool execution
options.body: Review and land the linked transport-level fix if maintainers accept `[DONE]` as the clean-stream terminal signal for native tool-call deltas.

options.title: Require exact-provider proof first
options.body: Keep the issue and PR open until a redacted Evolink or equivalent live-provider run proves the exact reported route after the fix.

options.title: Keep finish_reason required
options.body: Close or reject the fix path if maintainers want to keep requiring an explicit provider finish reason before streamed tool calls can execute.

recommendation.title: Accept clean-DONE tool execution
recommendation.body: Review and land the linked transport-level fix if maintainers accept `[DONE]` as the clean-stream terminal signal for native tool-call deltas.

likelyOwner.reason: He merged the adjacent non-tool-stop stripping behavior and is the clearest owner signal for accepting a widened execution boundary.
